3. Theoretical Frameworks to Enhance Gen Z Engagement and Performance

The increasing diversity and complexity of the modern workforce necessitate the adoption of theoretical frameworks that cater to the unique needs and preferences of Generation Z (Gen Z). This section explores two prominent theoretical frameworks that can enhance Gen Z engagement and performance: Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and Transformational Leadership.

1. Self-Determination Theory (SDT): A Multidimensional Approach to Enhancing Gen Z Engagement

Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan, 2000) posits that human behavior is motivated by three innate psychological needs: autonomy, competence, and relatedness. By incorporating these principles into organizational design, managers can foster a work environment that promotes Gen Z engagement and performance.

Autonomy: Empowerment through Flexible Work Models and Self-Directed Projects

Gen Z values flexibility and autonomy in the workplace (Katz & Krueger, 2016). By offering flexible work arrangements, such as telecommuting or flexible hours, organizations can provide employees with the autonomy to manage their work-life balance and increase job satisfaction (Golden & Veiga, 2005). Additionally, self-directed projects can enable employees to take ownership of their work, develop a sense of competence, and enhance their motivation (Amabile, 1993).

Competence: Opportunities for Continual Learning and Skill Development

Gen Z is characterized by a strong desire for lifelong learning and skill development (Pew Research Center, 2019). Organizations can foster a culture of competence by providing opportunities for employees to develop new skills, attend workshops and training sessions, and engage in mentorship programs (Erdogan & Latham, 2005). By investing in employee development, organizations can enhance job satisfaction, reduce turnover, and improve overall performance (Katz & Krueger, 2016).

Relatedness: Fostering a Supportive Workplace Culture that Promotes Collaboration

Gen Z values social connections and a sense of belonging in the workplace (Katz & Krueger, 2016). Organizations can promote relatedness by fostering a supportive workplace culture that encourages collaboration, open communication, and teamwork (Hackman & Johnson, 2013). By creating a sense of community, organizations can increase employee engagement, reduce stress, and improve overall well-being (Eisenberger et al., 1986).

2. Transformational Leadership: A Leadership Approach that Resonates with Gen Z

Transformational Leadership (Bass, 1985) is a leadership approach that emphasizes the importance of inspiring and motivating employees to achieve organizational goals. This approach resonates with Gen Z, who values authenticity, transparency, and a sense of purpose (Katz & Krueger, 2016).

Inspirational Motivation: Leaders who Articulate a Compelling Vision that Resonates with Gen Z's Values

Transformational leaders who articulate a compelling vision that resonates with Gen Z's values can inspire and motivate employees to achieve organizational goals (Bass, 1985). By communicating a clear and compelling vision, leaders can increase employee engagement, motivation, and job satisfaction (Hackman & Johnson, 2013).

Intellectual Stimulation: Encouraging Innovation and Critical Thinking

Gen Z values intellectual stimulation and the opportunity to engage in meaningful work (Pew Research Center, 2019). Organizations can encourage innovation and critical thinking by providing employees with autonomy, resources, and support (Amabile, 1993). By fostering a culture of innovation, organizations can increase employee engagement, creativity, and overall performance (Katz & Krueger, 2016).

Individualized Consideration: Attention to Individual Developmental Needs and Career Aspirations

Transformational leaders who provide individualized consideration can increase employee engagement, motivation, and job satisfaction (Erdogan & Latham, 2005). By attending to individual developmental needs and career aspirations, leaders can create a sense of purpose and meaning in the workplace, leading to increased employee engagement and performance (Hackman & Johnson, 2013).
